# Safe code review: 451 banned-Safe handling

**Mode:** a `<base>...<head>` range, committed work only. I ran every area myself and no second checker verified the findings, so this is a **draft and has no score**. The areas were not run as nine separate reviewer agents.

Scope: 11 files, +304 −101 · base `482232a` → `b89c202` (1 commit, clean tree)
Repo: safe-client-gateway · TypeScript/NestJS · vitest · biome and tsc checks · 10 stated rules (AGENTS.md) plus the R-001…R-030 review remarks · 9 of 9 areas apply

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **Ready to open the PR.** Nothing blocks it: 4 findings, all low priority (P3). |
| Score | none. No second reviewer checked the findings (0 of 4 checked). |
| What held it back | Missing 451 tests on 2 of the 3 datasources; repeated literal test strings and a copied loop. |
| Fix first | Finding 1: add the 451 case to the `ExportApi` spec. |

The core change is correct:
- `mapBannedSafeError` runs before `HttpErrorFactory.from` in every Transaction Service catch block:
  - all 37 calls in `TransactionApi` go through `mapError`
  - 3 of 3 in `SafeBalancesApi`
  - 1 of 1 in `ExportApi`
- `DataSourceErrorFilter` sends `exception.code` as the response status, so a 451 reaches the client unchanged.
- 451 does not trip the circuit breaker, which only counts status ≥ 500 (`network.module.ts:150`).
- Only 404s are cached, so a 451 is never cached.

## What this review did not cover
- No tests were run (you asked for read-only), so whether the new specs pass is not verified here.
- No independent checking or scoring was done. Nothing was written to `.git/safe-code-review/`, so the next run will not show a "since your last run" comparison.

If someone removes one of these wrappers, those endpoints go back to returning "An error occurred" and no test catches it. | Add a "should forward a banned-Safe error" case to `export-api.service.spec.ts`, and a collectibles 451 integration case. |

## Worth tidying (optional, no effect on the verdict)
- `transaction-api.service.spec.ts:70-81`: the new helper function sits between `const baseUrl` and the `let` declarations. Moving it above the `describe` would match how other specs lay out their local helpers.

Your call on this proposal: fix now, ticket, or skip. Silence counts as skip.

## Not sure about these
- **Upstream sends a 451 with `nonFieldErrors`:** `TransactionApi.mapError` would forward that message, because its first branch wins before `mapBannedSafeError` runs (`transaction-api.service.ts:1193-1204`). The linked upstream PR says banned Safes report `detail`, so today this is harmless.

## Ruled out
- **Helper location:** putting `banned-safe.helper.ts` and `constants.ts` under central `src/datasources/errors/` could look like it breaks the rule that `src/datasources/` is frozen. It doesn't:
  - that rule only forbids new API-client directories, and `errors/helpers/` already exists as shared infrastructure (it holds the constraint-error helpers);
  - putting it in a module would stop `balances` and `csv-export` from importing it, because modules may only import each other through `domain/`.
- **`unknown` → `unknown` signature (R-009):** this matches `HttpErrorFactory.from(source: unknown)` and the existing private `mapError`, and no caller has to cast the result.
- **SPDX headers:** present on all new files.
- **ARCHITECTURE.md:** it was updated to describe the new mapping.

## How this was produced
I read the diff line by line, then:
- checked every `httpErrorFactory.from` call site in the repo;
- traced the error path through `HttpErrorFactory`, `DataSourceErrorFilter`, the circuit breaker and the cache;
- grepped every spec that draws a random status code;
- checked the findings against the AGENTS.md rules and the `docs/agents/remarks.md` catalog.
